newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Maine details Skellerup NZ restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Maine details Skellerup NZ restructuring.

text.p: Maine Investments on Monday detailed the restructuring it plans for Skellerup New Zealand Ltd as part of its $40 milllion equity injection.

The restructuring, announced in a memorandum to Skellerup Finance bondholders, involves an option on the sale of Skellerup's retailing interests, Levenes and Palmers Garden, to a newly created offshoot of Maine -- Vermont Investments.
Skellerup Finance's debt will be cut immediately by $3 million to $230 million and by another $50 to $75 million in the short- to medium-term.

"Maine is satisifed that the injection of the present funding and financial support, coupled with organisational and associated changes, will see the group restored to a position where it can meet its financial commitments both in the short and long term."
It said it was likely that an ongoing review would lead to a significant writedown of goodwill.
Skellerup New Zealand is a diversified investment group bought for NZ$400 million in 1995.
Maine, owned by Goldman Sachs and Skellerup managers, is the majority shareholder in Skellerup and itself is partly debt financed via a Skellerup Finance bond issue NZSF08011000=NZ.
Skellerup's core businesses would be re-organised into two separate division, industrial (comprising the previous manufacturing and distribution divisions) and retail including Levenes and Palmers.
Mining company DML Contracting will be acquired by Vermont for $6 million.
The remaining DML assets will be retained and disposed and proceeds of the sale of these assets will be used to further reduce senior bank debt.

An affiliate company of Vermont will be granted an option to buy the retail division for $30 million, increasing at 10 percent per year compounded through to the date of the exercise, open until 2001.
Maine said Skellerup's performance had fallen well short of expectations.
The additional capital invested, all of which will rank behind bondholders, is being injected without seeking any concessions from the bondholders.
"It is being used primarily to fund working capital requirements of Maine's industrial and retail businesses, as well as to pay down $3 million of senior bank debt.
Up to $12 million will be specifically set aside as a buffer to support future debt servicing requirements of the group, including interest payments to bondholders.
Maine said that the restructuring is currently subject to final approvals from its banks.
In a background paper, Main said Skellerup's retail division had had a difficult year.
"Stuart Campbell, Chief Executive Retail, has taken this opportunity to reassess his personal priorities and has decided to return to the U.K."
A replacement would be found in due course, it added.
Bondholder consent of the restructuring is not required. Banks are expected to approve the restructuring, Maine said.
